lines.en: A lot of my friends that I grew up with were going to jail or ended up dead or shot in the streets.
lines.zh: 我一起長大的很多朋友，不是進了監獄，就是死了，或是在街頭被槍殺。

lines.en: So, I fell victim to doing illegal stuff.
lines.zh: 所以我也淪落到做違法的事。

lines.en: But it was the moment that we got arm robbed where I have a gun to my head now.
lines.zh: 但就在我們被持槍搶劫、槍口抵著我的頭的那一刻。

lines.en: And once I saw the barrel of that gun being pointed at me, that was the moment I noticed, okay, if I survive this, I'm going to become a comedian or die trying.
lines.zh: 當我看到那把槍的槍管對著我，那一刻我就明白了：好，如果我能活過這一關，我要當喜劇演員，不然就拚到死為止。

lines.en: My comedy comes from that place of a healing, wanting to make our situation better at home.
lines.zh: 我的喜劇來自一個療傷的地方，想讓我們家裡的狀況變好。

lines.en: Like one time I watched my brother get beat for wetting the bed. It was a lot.
lines.zh: 像有一次，我看著我哥因為尿床被打。那真的很嚴重。

lines.en: So I would always try to step in to try to be like a coping mechanism for him. Maybe it's my mom.
lines.zh: 所以我總是會想介入，試著成為他的一種調適方式。也可能是我媽。

lines.en: So I knew I was funny.
lines.zh: 所以我知道我很好笑。

lines.en: I knew I was very entertaining.
lines.zh: 我知道我很會娛樂別人。

lines.en: But it didn't hit me until like college.
lines.zh: 但直到大學我才真正意識到。

lines.en: And I started to figure out, okay, wow, all the people I look up to are all like comedic legends and I feel more connected to them than anything I've ever felt in my life.
lines.zh: 我開始想通：好，哇，我崇拜的人全都是喜劇傳奇，我跟他們的連結感，比我這輩子感受過的任何東西都強。

lines.en: That is my purpose. So, I left college. I went home.
lines.zh: 那就是我的使命。所以我離開大學，回家了。

lines.en: I wrote all these goals down on the sheet of paper. Now, I'm locked in.
lines.zh: 我把所有目標寫在一張紙上。從那時起，我全心投入。

lines.en: I have no other option.
lines.zh: 我沒有其他選擇。

lines.en: I'm sitting here in a room, no mattress. My car got repossessed.
lines.zh: 我坐在一個房間裡，連床墊都沒有。我的車被收回了。

lines.en: I actually made that like a content piece.
lines.zh: 我其實還把那件事拍成了內容。

lines.en: But I feared nothing because I'm like, I have nothing left.
lines.zh: 但我什麼都不怕，因為我覺得，我已經一無所有了。

lines.en: But I knew I'm like, I'm going to keep going.
lines.zh: 但我知道，我要繼續走下去。

lines.en: I'm going to continue to keep pursuing, making videos.

lines.en: You know, I've interviewed a lot of comedians and one of the things that I tend to find is that comedy is some sort of like tool.
lines.zh: 你知道，我訪問過很多喜劇演員，我常發現喜劇是某種工具。

lines.en: And when I spoke to Jimmy Carr or some of these other comedians that I've interviewed,
lines.zh: 我和 Jimmy Carr 或其他訪問過的喜劇演員聊的時候，

lines.zh: 他們總能理解，在早年的環境中，他們是如何用這個工具去解決自己當時遇到的問題。

lines.en: So I remember Jimmy saying to me, he goes, "You often think of comedians as being depressed, but actually for him it was a case of comedy was a way to help his mom who was depressed.
lines.zh: 我記得 Jimmy 跟我說：「大家常以為喜劇演員很憂鬱，但對他來說，喜劇其實是一種幫助他憂鬱的媽媽的方式。

lines.zh: 那是他讓媽媽笑的方式。」對。

lines.en: I I and I speak about my dad cuz he was one of those tough guys to deal with around that time.
lines.zh: 我會提到我爸，因為那時候他是個很難相處的硬漢。

lines.en: He wanted us to figure it out early and like my dad was like the lead person of pushing that narrative.
lines.zh: 他希望我們早早想清楚自己要做什麼，我爸就是那個最推這套說法的人。

lines.en: My mom somewhat would do it but she would always try to tell him relax.
lines.zh: 我媽多少也會這樣，但她總會試著叫他冷靜點。

lines.en: It's you know he's still he's still a kid like he's I'm at the time like 8 n years old and my dad was like what do you want to do?
lines.zh: 說他還只是個孩子，我那時大概八、九歲，我爸就問：你想做什麼？

lines.en: Figure it out. You're either going to go to jail, you find a a craft or or you're going to end up in a warehouse or something.

lines.en: You got to figure out um whatever you're going to do, or you go to the military, get your ass blown off.
lines.zh: 你得想清楚你要做什麼，不然就去當兵，被炸得屁股開花。

lines.en: And that was the only three options.

lines.en: He was always talking about we're going back to war. are we going back to war?

lines.en: And I'm like, what the Are we going to war?

lines.en: Like, so, so early on, he pushed that he wanted me to figure it out.
lines.zh: 所以很早的時候，他就一直逼我想清楚自己要做什麼。

lines.en: And he had great lessons, but his teaching skills was was very tough and physical.
lines.zh: 他教了很多很好的道理，但他的教法非常嚴厲、會動手。

lines.en: You know, he's old school.

lines.en: He's very old school about his teachings and how he goes about doing it.

lines.zh: 他以前老是問一些反問句，像是他會說：去拿一把十字螺絲起子給我，我就拿了一把一字的。

lines.en: He's like this is not a Phillips screwdriver. Bam. Upside the head.
lines.zh: 他就說：這不是十字螺絲起子。啪，往頭上打下去。

lines.en: Then my brother goes he's like I want you to go get me a Phillips screwdriver.
lines.zh: 然後我哥去，他說：我要你去拿一把十字螺絲起子給我。

lines.en: So that was like the immediate of teaching.

lines.en: It's not the best way of teaching.
lines.zh: 那不是最好的教育方式。

lines.en: And from an early age, I learned that
lines.zh: 我從很小的時候就學到，

lines.en: speaking to other people's fathers and parents, I learned that this is not a normal thing.
lines.zh: 跟別人的爸爸和爸媽聊過之後，我才知道這不是正常的事。

lines.en: And I didn't know that until we would go to like neighborhood parties and stuff and maybe my dad would be like, "Oh, these my boys right here."
lines.zh: 我一直不知道，直到我們去參加鄰居派對之類的，我爸可能會說：「喔，這是我的兒子們。」

lines.en: He'll reach out his hand and we'll flinch like that because it became a a normal thing for him to always lift up his hand like if we said the wrong thing.
lines.zh: 他一伸出手，我們就會像這樣縮一下，因為如果我們說錯話，他舉起手已經變成家常便飯了。

lines.en: So, I wouldn't say that my comedy necessarily came from that, but it definitely came from like a healing, wanting to make our situation better at home.
lines.zh: 所以我不會說我的喜劇一定是從那裡來的，但它確實來自療傷，想讓家裡的狀況變好。

lines.en: It's not like we we don't come from a like a broke home.

lines.zh: 我不會說我們不是破碎的家庭，我們確實是破碎的家庭。

lines.en: We weren't a broke home.
lines.zh: 但我們不是窮困的家庭。

lines.zh: 嗯，我媽在 CDC（美國疾病管制中心）工作。兩個都是很好的工作。

lines.en: Um, my mom was always home.
lines.zh: 嗯，我媽一直都在家。

lines.en: My dad would travel in and out.
lines.zh: 我爸會進進出出地飛。

lines.en: But I think what I wanted to do and my personality as a kid was always to make the family smile.
lines.zh: 但我覺得我小時候想做的、我的個性，一直都是讓家人笑。

lines.en: No matter through all this stuff that we're going through and these teachings being too far sometimes or maybe this ass whooping was too much,
lines.zh: 不管我們經歷了什麼，那些教育有時太過頭，或那頓打太過分了，

lines.en: the ass whooping went too far because I don't got I'm not going to get into details on here, but we had some ass whoopers in the house that went too far.
lines.zh: 那些打真的太過頭了，因為我不會在這裡講細節，但我們家有些打真的太過頭了。

lines.en: Um, but yeah, I think I I I feel like my comedy comes from that place of I never tend to punch down.
lines.zh: 嗯，但對，我覺得我的喜劇來自一個地方，就是我從不拿弱者開玩笑。

lines.en: I like to find the funny but also the good side of funny and not look at the negative for my type of comedy.
lines.zh: 我喜歡找出好笑的地方，但也是好的那種好笑，我的喜劇不看負面的東西。

lines.en: I can find a negative situation and bring the funny out of it for both sides, me and the other person.
lines.zh: 我可以在負面的情況裡，為雙方、為我和對方都找出好笑的地方。

lines.en: So, I I guess as a child, very perceptive children, you you're you're on edge a little bit then. For sure.
lines.zh: 所以我猜你小時候是個非常敏銳的孩子，那時候你會有點緊繃。沒錯。

lines.en: And it's funny cuz I remember sitting with Gabor Maté and him telling me how kids that have an early context where they are they have to be a little bit more
lines.zh: 這很有趣，因為我記得和 Gabor Maté 聊過，他說早年環境讓孩子必須更……

lines.en: um aware. Yeah. They often become very good at observation. Yes.
lines.zh: 嗯，更警覺的話。對。這些孩子常常變得很會觀察。對。

lines.en: And they very they become good therapists.
lines.zh: 而且他們很會……他們會變成很好的治療師。

lines.en: They become the most empathetic.
lines.zh: 他們會變成最有同理心的人。

lines.en: They also sometimes have struggles with mental health because being hypervigilant or being aware comes at a cost. It's not free.
lines.zh: 他們有時也會有心理健康的困擾，因為過度警覺、時時提防是有代價的。那不是免費的。

lines.en: For all the upsides, there's always a downside.
lines.zh: 所有的好處，總有它的壞處。

lines.en: Does any of that resonate? 1,000%, man.
lines.zh: 這些有引起你的共鳴嗎？百分之一千，兄弟。

lines.en: And I think sadly in my brother's case, that went a negative direction.
lines.zh: 而我覺得很遺憾，在我哥身上，它往負面的方向發展了。

lines.en: He was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder as we continued to go through puberty and got older.
lines.zh: 隨著我們進入青春期、年紀漸長，他被診斷出思覺失調症和雙極性疾患。

lines.en: Whereas for me, I feel like I might have found a coping mechanism with comedy and maybe he never found that coping mechanism from that trauma.
lines.zh: 而我覺得我可能在喜劇裡找到了一種調適方式，他也許從來沒有找到面對那些創傷的調適方式。

lines.en: And I feel like trauma can sometimes give you the the good route or the negative route.
lines.zh: 我覺得創傷有時會帶你走上好的路，也可能走上負面的路。

lines.en: And I feel like a lot of that going on in our house early on may have played a role in him being diagnosed with that.
lines.zh: 我覺得我們家早年發生的很多事，可能在他被診斷出這些病上扮演了某種角色。

lines.en: And yeah, that's the that's the sad side of the story.
lines.zh: 對，那就是這個故事令人難過的一面。

lines.en: But yeah, I I even with him like I think early on I would always try to make him laugh because I knew we were in a up situation.
lines.zh: 但對，就算是對他，我想早年我也總是試著逗他笑，因為我知道我們的處境很糟。

lines.en: One time I watched my brother get beat for wetting the bed and it was the simplest thing and I couldn't understand.
lines.zh: 有一次我看著我哥因為尿床被打，那是最小的一件事，我無法理解。

lines.en: I was like why is he like like getting beat this bad?
lines.zh: 我想：為什麼他要被打得這麼慘？

lines.en: It was very far very not the normal belt type thing.
lines.zh: 那真的太過頭了，完全不是一般用皮帶打那種。

lines.en: It was very very far.

lines.en: Find a trade. Yeah. But until you have you're given a word for it sometimes.

lines.en: I thought that about like being an entrepreneur.
lines.zh: 我對當創業家也有這種感覺。

lines.en: I didn't know it was a thing until I was 19 and I was already doing it and then I heard the word and someone gave it meaning.
lines.zh: 我直到 19 歲才知道有這回事，那時我已經在做了，然後我聽到這個詞，有人給了它意義。

lines.en: I was like oh that's a thing you can do as a job. Yeah.
lines.zh: 我才想：喔，這是可以當工作的。對。

lines.en: And then suddenly you know mind expansion. Yeah.
lines.zh: 然後突然，你知道，眼界就打開了。對。

lines.en: You know what it was?
lines.zh: 你知道那是什麼嗎？

lines.en: I I knew I always knew that comedy was a thing.
lines.zh: 我一直都知道喜劇這回事。

lines.en: I didn't know that I wanted to do it as bad as I was doing it.
lines.zh: 我只是不知道我這麼想做這件事。

lines.en: I was always watching it.
lines.zh: 我一直都在看。

lines.en: I always watched My mom would show us in Living Color movies like What About Bob? early on.
lines.zh: 我一直都在看，我媽很早就會給我們看《In Living Color》，還有像《天才也瘋狂（What About Bob?）》這種電影。

lines.en: My dad would always have the Chappelle show on and I would try to sneak and watch that because I was very like much rated R.
lines.zh: 我爸總是開著《Chappelle's Show》，我會偷偷去看，因為那很像限制級。

lines.en: In the kids' mind, they would they'd be like, "Oh, you can't watch this stuff. Get upstairs."
lines.zh: 在小孩的腦袋裡，大人會說：「喔，你不能看這種東西，上樓去。」

lines.en: And I would still try to sneak behind the stairs and look like, "Oh my god, that's so funny."
lines.zh: 我還是會偷偷躲在樓梯後面看，想說：「天啊，這好好笑。」

lines.en: And I would try to say these jokes back at school that I hear Dave Chappelle saying or blank man like he was like he was
lines.zh: 我會試著在學校重複我聽到 Dave Chappelle 講的笑話，或是《Blankman》，他就像……

lines.en: like a guy in a wheelchair from Living Color that ended up becoming a movie and they made this whole thing called Blake.
lines.zh: 《In Living Color》裡一個坐輪椅的角色，後來變成一部電影，他們做了一整個叫 Blankman 的東西。

lines.en: But the fact of the matter is that I it was always in front of me and I always was a big fan of comedy.
lines.zh: 但事實是，喜劇一直都在我眼前，我也一直是喜劇的大粉絲。

lines.en: I just didn't know that my mom sort of to say was influencing and she and and I say my mom because she would always put this stuff in front of us
lines.zh: 我只是不知道，可以這麼說，我媽一直在影響我，我說我媽，是因為她總是把這些東西擺在我們面前，

lines.en: because she wanted she wanted the best for us but she always she she was the like almost like the seessaw to level everything out if something bad happens with my dad.
lines.zh: 因為她希望我們好，但她總是……她幾乎就像蹺蹺板，如果我爸那邊發生了什麼不好的事，她會把一切拉平。

lines.en: My mom was always there to level it out.
lines.zh: 我媽總是在那裡把事情拉平。

lines.en: She was the one that would come in and tell him like, "David, that's too much."
lines.zh: 她就是那個會進來跟他說：「David，這太過分了。」的人。

lines.en: And sometimes he would bark at her and be like, "Get the out of here."
lines.zh: 有時候他會對她吼：「給我滾出去。」

lines.en: Like, "These boys are going to end up being men.
lines.zh: 「這些男孩以後要成為男人。

lines.en: They need to learn this now."
lines.zh: 他們現在就得學會這些。」

lines.en: But she always had like quotes or or or good things she would always say like, "Just just continue to believe in yourself. Continue to know this."
lines.zh: 但她總是有一些名言或好話，像是：「就繼續相信你自己。繼續記得這一點。」

lines.en: So, she was my mom was always a big believer in anything becoming big, you know. Yeah.
lines.zh: 所以我媽一直都很相信任何事都能成就大事，你知道。對。

lines.en: So, I got to I got to give her a lot for that.
lines.zh: 所以這點我真的要給她很大的功勞。
